recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up core source work is recommended for FHIR-13519 unless PA opens a new, specific editorial issue to revise additional Practitioner element definitions beyond the already-correct qualification definition.
issue_request: FHIR-13519 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Administration change request for STU3 Practitioner definitions. It asked for better Practitioner property definitions because short and long definitions were often the same or circular, specifically noting that Practitioner.qualification did not make clear what a qualification is and should include examples of appropriate content. The accepted resolution was to update descriptions as requested.
initial_application: The issue was applied by git commit 85a500a375a412882d3967105ce8ada6d8ce728b, "GF#13519 - Need better definitions (for practitioner properties)", which changed source/practitioner/practitioner-spreadsheet.xml from a terse Practitioner.qualification short description to an expanded short description and added a long definition with a medical-license example. That spreadsheet source was later refactored into the current StructureDefinition XML representation.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Practitioner as an active resource owned by PA. Later final PA issues refined the same qualification area: FHIR-19961 added qualification/licensure wording, FHIR-25033 added the PractitionerRole.specialty distinction comment, FHIR-36681 narrowed qualification.identifier wording, and FHIR-34375 added qualification.status and period guidance. A scan still finds some self-evident Practitioner short/definition pairs differing only by punctuation, but Practitioner.qualification itself is not one of them, and a broader duplicate-definition issue, FHIR-31798, is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current Practitioner.qualification short and long definitions, example, and comment already satisfy the seed issue; rewriting unrelated self-evident definitions would be broader editorial work rather than a necessary FHIR-13519 correction.
